LESSON: VERSE

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS
Strand: Creating and Performing
Topic 2.8: Verse

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Verse. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can verse performance be made interesting and memorable?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe language use in verse
2. compose a verse to address an issue in society
3. perform a verse before an audience

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: VERSE
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Verse helps you succeed in CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: VERSE
Study Verse like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Describe language use in verse

What this means
In this part you learn to describe language use in verse. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe language use in verse.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Verse” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe language use in verse. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Compose a verse to address an issue in society

What this means
In this part you learn to compose a verse to address an issue in society. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: compose a verse to address an issue in society.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Verse in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can compose a verse to address an issue in society. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Perform a verse before an audience

What this means
In this part you learn to perform a verse before an audience. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: perform a verse before an audience.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can perform a verse before an audience. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Verse is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Verse” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: describe language use in verse)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Verse in your own words. (skill: compose a verse to address an issue in society)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: perform a verse before an audience)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Verse to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe language use in verse.
3. Practise this skill: compose a verse to address an issue in society.
4. Practise this skill: perform a verse before an audience.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Verse from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Verse: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Verse?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can verse performance be made interesting and memorable?
2. Why is it important to decorate props to be used for performance?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Verse means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe language use in verse.
5. Be able to: compose a verse to address an issue in society.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
